subject: Request: Escalation for Crestline termination / ramp language (exec approval needed)
message_1:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Deal Desk <dealdesk@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: Escalation for Crestline termination / ramp language (exec approval needed)

Team —

Crestline Health (Nina Patel) has asked for the ability to opt out of the committed ramp between months 4–6 if utilization is <40% for two consecutive months. They want that opt-out to translate into a pro-rated termination with a credit back rather than being treated as a breach. They also requested explicit "ramp staircase" language that reduces minimums over time.

Quick context: this is a 24-month committed plan, $1.2M ARR run rate if fully ramped. They are a strategic healthcare prospect in our east coast pilot program (sensitive PHI, private deployment considered). Procurement flagged the opt-out as a blocker for legal/finance.

What I'm asking for:
- Exec guidance on whether we can permit an early-termination-as-opt-out construct (non-breach) for the ramp window;
- A recommended cap for credits (absolute $ cap vs % of remaining commitment);
- Any required signoffs (Finance / Legal / Security) we should include before offering.

Attached: Crestline_SOW_v2.pdf and an initial ramp language draft (ramp_language_draft.docx) with two proposals (gradual staircase and one-step opt-out).

Goal: If we can get exec approval to offer a limited opt-out with clear caps and audit triggers, sales can close this quarter. If not, we need to present a firmer "no opt-out" position to procurement.

Thanks —
Lauren Bishop
Senior Sales Manager, East
Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com
[Attachment: Crestline_SOW_v2.pdf] [Attachment: ramp_language_draft.docx]
message_2:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Deal Desk <dealdesk@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: Escalation for Crestline termination / ramp language (exec approval needed)

Lauren —

Thanks for the clear ask and the SOW. My take is we can accommodate a controlled opt-out for the ramp period but only with three guardrails:

1) Graduated ramp schedule (preferred):
   - Month 1: 100% committed capacity applies
   - Month 2: 75% commit
   - Month 3: 50% commit
   - Months 4–6: Customer may elect opt-out if utilization < 40% for two consecutive months (notification window: 30 days)

2) Credit cap: limit to the lesser of 20% of remaining committed value or $150,000 (absolute cap). Credits are calculated as pro-rated unused months at the effective rate and will be net of any usage invoiced.

3) Audit and data clause: opt-out can only be triggered if audit logs / telemetry (token counts, session counts) confirm low usage; Security must sign off on telemetry sources.

I attached a short clean clause (ramp_language_draft.docx, section B) for legal to quick-redline. This keeps the customer flexible while protecting our committed economics.

Risks: sets a precedent for future pilots; could increase churn if we let customers walk without a significant cap.

If you want, propose we ask for a one-time "onboarding success review" KPI at month 2 tied to a professional services checkpoint (optional).

- Marissa
Director, Deal Desk
[Attachment: ramp_language_draft.docx]

Approving the limited opt-out with conditions. Executive decision and conditions below — please treat as final for this deal only: 

Decision: APPROVE the graduated ramp + opt-out construct with the following conditions

1) Credit cap: $150,000 absolute cap on any opt-out credit. No exceptions.
2) Auditability: Opt-out only triggered if the named telemetry sources (token_counts, session_durations, active_user_ids) confirm utilization < 40% for two consecutive months. Security/IR must sign off on telemetry collection prior to contract execution.
3) PS checkpoint: Professional Services work required at month 2. This will be billed on T&M and must be accepted by customer in SOW.
4) Private deployment clause: Customer must sign the DPA and attest to onboarding timeline; opt-out tied only to private deployment run.
5) Finance will negotiate billing schedule changes but will not amortize credits beyond calendar quarter close.

Next steps: Legal will insert the approved clause (use Marissa's draft as baseline). Lauren, please get counterparty acceptance and ensure Crestline executes the DPA + PS order. Once we have signatures, Finance will prepare the true-up schedule and I will sign the final offer.

Aditya Rao
Chief Revenue Officer, Redwood Inference
